newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB sticks to 0.5 pct Swiss 1997 GDP growth - Meyer.
newsitem.headline: SNB sticks to 0.5 pct Swiss 1997 GDP growth - Meyer.

text.p: Swiss National Bank (SNB) chairman Hans Meyer said the central bank was maintaining its forecast that the Swiss economy would grow 0.5 percent in 1997 despite downward revisions of estimates by leading think tanks.
"The situation is without doubt serious, but not dramatic," Meyer told the SonntagsZeitung weekly in an interview published on Sunday.
"The propsects for the current year are subdued. A certain recovery is foreseen only for 1998," he said, adding, "We are sticking to our forecast of 0.5 percent growth."

He said low inflation, relatively low interest rates and the Swiss franc's downward correction against major currencies had set the stage for recovery after six years of economic stagnation, and that structural adjustments were far along.
But the economy needed a boost from exports because of weak domestic demand, Meyer said.
"As always, we have to wait for a spark from abroad, especially from continental Europe," he said.
Economists believe gross domestic product contracted by 0.6 percent last year after rising a scant 0.1 percent in 1995.

Meyer welcomed the government's plan to launch a 550 million Swiss franc ($385 million) financial stimulus package that, if matched by contributions from cantonal and local governments, could boost spending on infrastructure projects by 1.8 billion this year.
Berne was still maintaining its goal of reducing budget deficits, he said, but added he would like to see more emphasis on increasing competition.
He dismissed suggestions that deflation was a major worry.

"I am not so pessimistic about deflation because we have supplied money generously since mid-1995," he said. "And Switzerland's fiscal policy is overall not restrictive, even if the public sector's efforts to save are often seen in this way."
Meyer said he expected the domestic real estate market to remain weak through the end of the century, underscoring risk-sensitive banks' tough credit conditions.
"This concerns me, but I am not afraid of dramtic developments as in Japan," he said.
He reiterated the SNB forecast from December of one percent inflation in 1997. ($1=1.4260 Swiss Franc)
